value.body: A three-year MD after MBBS in diagnosing disease through laboratory work — histopathology, cytology, haematology, clinical pathology and blood banking. Pathologists work in hospital labs, diagnostic chains, blood banks and medical colleges. Most of the work is lab-based, with limited direct patient contact.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: MBBS with a completed internship and NMC/State Medical Council registration. Admission is through NEET-PG; seats are filled by MCC counselling (All-India quota, central and deemed universities) and by state counselling. DNB Pathology through NBEMS is a parallel route.

value.title: At a glance
items: The routine is usually more predictable than in emergency-based specialties, though large labs run shifts.
Setting up an independent lab needs capital and accreditation; many pathologists work in hospital or chain labs.
Common next steps are senior residency, medical-college teaching, or a fellowship in areas such as haematopathology or cytopathology.
